harness.note: The better-borg-c runner and observer at this commit build and run every specimen. A specimen is the game and Borg source at its own ref; the observer instrumentation comes from the harness commit. It applies to specimens of kind "better-borg-c" (the default). Specimens of kind "borg-rs" are built and run by borg-rs's own harness at the specimen's ref (harness/build.sh and the borgh frontend). This pin is also a specimen ref (4.2.6-bbc-9ca98661): the harness bumped with the mode-cutoff restart so runner and specimens move together (borg-zoo#54).

experiment.prespecified: Fixed 2026-11-24, before any result (Rule 22, #758). Pilot classes-18, retained evidence, normal world; the breeder world runs as its own experiment (reborn-guards-inv-breeders). The walkoff arm exposes the guard-vs-walk-away ordering, not walk-away as a play style (owner: NEVER off, the index row stands). Gate: no config_error; one binary; each arm's values in params-core.json; every cell ends in death, turn_cap or borg_stopped; identical plays per arm. Progress endpoint CL5 reached by 100,000 turns - known attainment out of all starts, deaths, unfinished and alive at the cutoff with CL5 reported separately; DL3/DL5 and level arrival as diagnostics. Report: deaths and causes; paired CL5 gained and lost over pairs known in both arms (exact McNemar); the fire inventory - for every diverging pair, which guard acted (re-entry hold after its ticks; oscillation limit at its cap), on which grid, at which CL/DL, and what the guardsoff game did instead - reconstructed from the retained notes; named cases (/death-report) for every diverging pair that ends in a death; and the ordering question (when a retreat target is also walk-away-forbidden, which rule wins) from the retained keys plus a source read at the pinned commit. Descriptive (RULES 14). A ladder only after this read, on the owner's word.
